name: Epithelioid Trophoblastic Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Epithelioid Trophoblastic Tumor

criteria.description: Presence of monomorphic epithelioid trophoblastic cells arranged in nests and sheets with eosinophilic cytoplasm and geographic necrosis
Positive staining for p63, cytokeratin 18, and human placental lactogen (hPL) with negative or focal hCG expression
History of prior gestational event (e.g., pregnancy, molar pregnancy, abortion) within preceding years
Serum beta-hCG levels elevated but typically lower than in choriocarcinoma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with characteristic immunohistochemical profile is required; clinical history and serum beta-hCG levels support diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires expert pathological review due to overlap with other trophoblastic tumors.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pelvic mass detected on examination or imaging
searchTerms: pelvic lump found on exam or scan

common.symptomName: Elevated serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) levels
searchTerms: high blood levels of beta-hCG hormone

common.notes: Due to tumor mass effect or invasion

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms such as weight loss or malaise
searchTerms: general symptoms like weight loss or tiredness

occasional.symptomName: Metastatic symptoms including cough or hemoptysis
searchTerms: symptoms from metastases like cough or coughing blood

occasional.notes: If tumor invades bladder or urinary tract
Due to mass effect or ascites

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms such as headache or seizures
rare.notes: If central nervous system metastases occur
searchTerms: headache or seizures from neurological involvement
skin bumps due to tumor spread

rare.notes: Paraneoplastic syndrome due to hCG cross-reactivity

laboratory: Elevated human placental lactogen (hPL) in tumor tissue
Normal or mildly elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing heterogeneous uterine mass
MRI pelvis demonstrating well-circumscribed tumor with necrosis
Chest CT scan for pulmonary metastases
genetic: Tumor shows gestational origin confirmed by DNA polymorphism analysis
other: Histopathology with monomorphic epithelioid trophoblastic cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for p63 and cytokeratin 18

distinguishingFeatures: Biphasic population of cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast cells
Predominantly intermediate trophoblastic cells with infiltrative growth

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging uterine mass with abnormal bleeding
Elevated but disproportionate serum beta-hCG levels
Evidence of metastatic disease on imaging
references: Shih IM. Epithelioid trophoblastic tumor: a review. Arch Pathol Lab Med. 2015;139(6):802-806.
